deckType: Romance craft deck — writing mechanics as performative card game
bundleSuggestion: Love & Relational Wreckage bundle (pair with Love, Bonding & Other Dangerous Constructs)

cards.power: Force opponent to reveal their character's greatest strength. It instantly triggers your character's worst flaw.
cards.lore: Attraction is no accident. It's a collision. Strengths and weaknesses must violently clash to create the narrative spark.
cards.gradeReason: Strength-reveals-flaw mechanic is instantly embodied. You know exactly what to write.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Punk raccoon and elegant swan colliding mid-air, sparks flying. Mood: Magnetic chaos.

cards.power: Attach to a wounded fighter. Their weakness becomes your healing potential, generating +3 Chemistry Tokens.
cards.lore: You don't complete me, you fix my specific psychological damage. No friction structure? No drama. Just decoration.
cards.gradeReason: Wound-as-healing-vector is a specific, playable move. Not decorative — weaponized.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Bandaged goat leaning on a limping fox, both holding each other up. Mood: Tender dependency.

cards.power: Play when both players discard a card. Bind both characters to the exact same past trauma.
cards.lore: The ultimate resonance point. They suffer the same damage, but developed opposite false survival mechanisms.
cards.gradeReason: Same trauma, opposite coping — that's a writeable scene immediately. Perfect resonance mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with blood-red watercolor. Subject: Two wolves with identical scars facing opposite directions. Mood: Devastating symmetry.

cards.power: Trap Card. Discard any couple that looks 'perfectly matched' on paper. They take 5 Boredom Damage.
cards.lore: Perfection is the enemy of the Love Epic. If they don't challenge each other existentially, tear up the script.
cards.gradeReason: '5 Boredom Damage' for the perfect couple is comedy and craft doctrine in one move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Two identical golden retrievers in matching outfits, flat smiles, surrounding rubble. Mood: Polished catastrophe.

cards.power: Discard all your Defense shields. Gain the "True Love" win condition.
cards.lore: The Contemporary Romance thesis. You cannot be loved until you drop the mask. It's an ethical bloodbath. (Architects Daughter)
cards.gradeReason: Clear thesis but 'ethical bloodbath' lore is more slogan than instruction. Still playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Armadillo shedding its shell in open field, completely exposed. Mood: Terrified liberation.

cards.power: Cancel an enemy's attack, but you must permanently discard your highest-damage weapon.
cards.lore: The Second-Chance Mandate. To rebuild trust, you must abandon the safety of your grudges. (Architects Daughter)
cards.gradeReason: Permanent weapon sacrifice as cost of forgiveness is solid. 'Second-Chance Mandate' slightly label-y.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Bear lowering a club, a fox handing back a stolen item. Mood: Costly peace.

cards.power: Expose all hidden cards in your opponent's hand. The most embarrassing one becomes their core identity.
cards.lore: The RomCom Imperative. The most embarrassing, pants-down moment of one's life becomes their core identity. (Architects Daughter)
cards.gradeReason: 'Most embarrassing card becomes core identity' — players instantly know the scene to write.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Chameleon caught mid-color-change, all camouflage failing simultaneously. Mood: Mortified revelation.

cards.power: Destroy the current Arena. The lovers survive, but society is discarded.
cards.lore: Historical and Paranormal law. Individual love over collective expectation. The world burns, the heart beats. (Architects Daughter)
cards.gradeReason: 'The world burns, the heart beats' — best lore line on this page. Immediate dramatic instruction.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with fire-orange watercolor. Subject: Two lovers running from a crumbling palace, holding hands. Mood: Glorious arson.

cards.gradeReason: Power/lore text partially obscured by visual at reading resolution. Hamster-treadmill concept is descriptive, not immediately performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Two hamsters on separate treadmills, glancing at each other exhaustedly. Mood: Modern romantic paralysis.

cards.power: Convert an opponent's quirky points into Humor tokens.
cards.lore: Humor as a valve for the fear of love. Don't use slapstick as decoration—use it to completely expose a character's core flaw.
cards.gradeReason: Good doctrine but 'quirky points → Humor tokens' is abstract without context. Lore saves it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Pelican slipping on a banana peel, papers flying, another animal watching in mortified attraction. Mood: Farcical yearning.

cards.power: Block all communication. Can only be resolved by character growth, not a simple text message.
cards.lore: No artificial drama! True misunderstandings must grow logically out of the characters' false protection mechanisms.
cards.gradeReason: 'Can only be resolved by character growth, not a text message' — brilliant rule. Immediately functional.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Owl and cat facing opposite walls, STATIC speech bubble between them. Mood: Excruciating proximity.

cards.power: Ignore all Emotional Damage this turn, but your character makes zero progress toward intimacy.
cards.lore: Jokes are armor. The witty banter isn't just fun, it's a desperate tactic to avoid being truly vulnerable.
cards.gradeReason: Zero intimacy progress as cost of humor armor — perfect mechanic for the comic-deflector character type.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Hyena holding a comedic mask as shield, arrows bouncing off, heart locked behind. Mood: Defensive hilarity.

cards.power: Lock a character's actions to 'Society Rules'. They cannot attack directly.
cards.lore: Dialogue that sounds ironical but hits modern emotional truth. Societal constraint is the physical architecture of the cage.
cards.gradeReason: Solid historical romance mechanic. 'Societal constraint as physical architecture' is good but slightly academic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with sepia watercolor. Subject: Badger in Victorian dress trapped in an ornate gilded cage. Mood: Constrained longing.

cards.power: The player with higher Power must voluntarily reduce their stats to zero to allow the romance to progress.
cards.lore: Power imbalance requires sacrifice. The stronger entity must intentionally weaken themselves, or it's just a power-fantasy, not a romance.
cards.gradeReason: Stronger entity must self-weaken — immediately playable rule for vampire/demon/supernatural romance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with purple watercolor. Subject: Massive wolf deliberately kneeling before a small rabbit, fangs retracted. Mood: Chosen vulnerability.

cards.power: Resurrect a discarded relationship, but pay double the initial emotional cost.
cards.lore: The second chance must be more expensive than the first. The characters must risk infinitely more this time.
cards.gradeReason: Double cost mechanic is perfect — instantly tells writers the second chance must hurt more than the first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Dog and troll holding a cracked vase together, both visibly terrified. Mood: Costly resurrection.

cards.power: Convert Trauma tokens into Attraction. Highly unstable.
cards.lore: Sex as a power struggle, healing, or destruction. Morally risky, but legitimate if the trauma is followed to its darkest consequence.
cards.gradeReason: Trauma-to-Attraction conversion is interesting. 'Highly unstable' and 'morally risky' hedges slightly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with dark watercolor. Subject: Two shadowy panthers circling each other in a stone dungeon. Mood: Dangerous magnetism.

cards.power: High competence in the outer world, zero defense in the love arena.
cards.lore: Hero: Highly competent externally, totally vulnerable in love. Must learn: "I am enough, even without the mask."
cards.gradeReason: The character brief in nine words: 'High competence outside, zero defense in love.' Instantly embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with Komika Axis lettering. Subject: Regal lion in business suit, heart exposed through chest. Mood: Armored and naked simultaneously.

cards.power: Perfectly targets the Protagonist's specific psychological wound.
cards.lore: Complementary perfection. Must have their own wound (fear of commitment, false loyalty) or they are just a prop.
cards.gradeReason: Good functional definition. 'Or they are just a prop' is the key warning. Slightly functional rather than inviting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Sheep with a hidden scar, looking directly at a lion off-frame. Mood: Targeted tenderness.

cards.power: Tempts the Protagonist with safety. Delays the HEA indefinitely.
cards.lore: The Ex, the Career, the Society. Never a pure villain—they inevitably create the temptation of safety over the terrifying work of true love.
cards.gradeReason: Solid antagonist brief. 'Never a pure villain' is crucial doctrine. Lore is more explanatory than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Walrus in expensive suit gesturing to a comfortable sofa, protagonist wavering. Mood: Seductive mediocrity.

cards.power: Forces a player to read their character's hidden flaw out loud.
cards.lore: Not just comic relief, the mirror, telling the protagonist the brutal truth they desperately refuse to hear.
cards.gradeReason: 'Forces a player to read their character's hidden flaw out loud' — literally performative. Table gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Wise tortoise holding a mirror to a reluctant rabbit's face. Mood: Uncomfortable clarity.

cards.power: Both players draw a card. Neither wins completely. Tension increases by +2.
cards.lore: Rhetorical sparring. Shows intelligence and attraction simultaneously. A power dynamic where neither side surrenders.
cards.gradeReason: Neither wins, tension builds — mechanically captures flirting perfectly. Zero-sum until it isn't.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Two foxes crossing verbal swords, both smirking, neither yielding. Mood: Electric standoff.

cards.power: Play when both characters are right. No black-and-white villains allowed.
cards.lore: The hardest debate to write. Conflict born from colliding, equally legitimate moral values. Nobody is screaming; everyone is bleeding.
cards.gradeReason: 'Nobody is screaming; everyone is bleeding' — instant masterclass in conflict writing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with storm-grey watercolor. Subject: Two rams locking horns on a cliff edge, both dignified. Mood: Devastating mutual rightness.

cards.power: Silence all inner monologues. Force characters to rely entirely on physical micro-expressions.
cards.lore: The moment the fight drops. Fewer words, more pauses. The character stops performing and simply is.
cards.gradeReason: No inner monologue, only micro-expressions — immediately tells the writer exactly what to write.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with soft watercolor. Subject: Two animals sitting in silence, watching each other breathe, broken hearts visible. Mood: Naked stillness.

cards.power: Expose the opponent's core wound and instantly heal it with exact, terrifying precision.
cards.lore: No clichés! The speech proves one thing: that you have truly, deeply seen the specific damage of the other person.
cards.gradeReason: 'Exact, terrifying precision' — this is the entire standard for the airport speech. Writers know their job.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with golden watercolor. Subject: Peacock mid-declaration, feathers fully open, opponent visibly disarmed. Mood: Surgical tenderness.

cards.power: Transfer Dominance from one character to the other. Creates new Vulnerability.
cards.lore: Erotica rule #1: Show the shift. Dominance to equality to surrender. Physical details are merely tools for emotional truth.
cards.gradeReason: Dominance transfer as vulnerability creation — clean, embodied, writeable immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Badger and squirrel on a seesaw, midpoint of crossing. Mood: Suspended power exchange.

cards.power: Smash one psychological barrier, immediately replace it with a new emotional vulnerability.
cards.lore: Erotica rule #2: Intimacy as an act of bravery, capitulation, a transgression of limits.
cards.gradeReason: Break one barrier, gain a new vulnerability — perfect ratchet mechanic. Intimacy escalates correctly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Rhinoceros charging through a stone wall, exposing a fragile interior. Mood: Cathartic breach.

cards.power: After intimacy, generate a massive new internal conflict based on the characters' flaws.
cards.lore: Erotica rule #3: Closeness breeds terror. Intimacy inevitably creates the fear of loss. That fear is your next plot point.
cards.gradeReason: 'Fear of loss is your next plot point' — perfect instruction. Writers know exactly where to go post-scene.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with warm then cold watercolor. Subject: Hedgehog curled protectively after emerging from another's embrace. Mood: Post-intimacy panic.

cards.power: The character gains Distance but takes Healing Damage.
cards.lore: Write from vulnerability, not performance. If it's just pornography with a plot, Uncle FrizzleBob disqualifies you.
cards.gradeReason: 'FrizzleBob disqualifies you' is funny but Distance + Healing Damage mechanic needs token context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Octopus retreating into shadow while trailing glowing ink. Mood: Necessary withdrawal.

cards.power: Remove all protective distance. Characters must confront each other's mundane reality.
cards.lore: The realm of the everyday. No grand ballrooms to hide in, just the terrifying vulnerability of making coffee.
cards.gradeReason: 'Terrifying vulnerability of making coffee' — specific, writeable scene. Not metaphor, actual location.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with morning watercolor. Subject: Raccoon and cat making coffee in a tiny kitchen, no escape route. Mood: Claustrophobic domesticity.

cards.power: Pit public expectation directly against private desire.
cards.lore: Architecture as a weapon. The physical space must map the exact tension axis of the relationship.
cards.gradeReason: 'Map the exact tension axis' is slightly academic. Strong concept but craft-lecture tone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with baroque watercolor. Subject: Two characters dancing formally in a grand ballroom, whispering intimately. Mood: Public facade, private fire.

cards.power: Apply "Summer" modifier: Maximum intensity, zero patience.
cards.lore: Spring is hope, winter is isolation, fall is maturity. Summer is pure, suffocating escalation. The weather is your feelings.
cards.gradeReason: 'Maximum intensity, zero patience' — apply it. Immediately deployable seasonal modifier.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with scorched orange watercolor. Subject: Lizard on hot pavement mid-argument with iguana. Mood: Heat-amplified emotional crisis.

cards.power: Manifest societal constraints as literal, impassable geography.
cards.lore: In Historical and Gothic, the house is the enemy. The social rules are built directly into the bricks.
cards.gradeReason: Good doctrine for Gothic/historical writers but 'impassable geography' is abstract to new writers.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with gothic watercolor. Subject: Koala navigating labyrinthine stone stairs with locked doors. Mood: Architecturally imprisoned.

cards.power: Trigger an inevitable encounter that exploits both characters' core flaws simultaneously.
cards.lore: Not just cute—fated. This encounter MUST force this specific character to face this specific opponent.
cards.gradeReason: 'MUST force this specific character to face this specific opponent' — plot test in one sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Badger and raccoon colliding at a crossroads, grocery bags exploding. Mood: Fated disaster.

cards.power: Force the characters to question if the emotional risk is worth the inevitable pain.
cards.lore: The midpoint shift. The realization that continuing this relationship will require destroying their old identity.
cards.gradeReason: 'Continuing requires destroying their old identity' — exact midpoint instruction. Writers know what scene to write.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with grey watercolor. Subject: Frog at a crossroads in rain, looking at a crumbling bridge. Mood: Irreversible threshold.

cards.power: Reactivate the original trauma. The false protection mechanism falls catastrophically.
cards.lore: The darkest hour. The false protection mechanism falls catastrophically. The trauma is real, and the loss feels permanent.
cards.gradeReason: 'The loss feels permanent' — three-word instruction for the writer. Darkest moment rendered as mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with black watercolor. Subject: All the gathered pieces of a life scattered in rubble. Mood: Earned devastation.

cards.power: Sacrifice your ego to provide exactly what the other character needs, not what they want.
cards.lore: Anti-Cliché Rule: Help instead of a speech. Heal the exact wound, nothing else.
cards.gradeReason: 'What they need, not what they want' — immediately writeable. Anti-airport-speech doctrine in one rule.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Frog carrying a lamp into the other character's darkness — no roses, just light. Mood: Surgical selflessness.

cards.power: Win the game. Can only be played if both core flaws have been actively sacrificed.
cards.lore: A Happy Ending isn't given, it's extracted from your flaws. It is the dramaturgical reward for learning vulnerability.
cards.gradeReason: 'Can only be played if both core flaws have been actively sacrificed' — the entire Happy Ending doctrine.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with golden watercolor. Subject: Two scarred animals standing together on a summit, wounds visible, smiling. Mood: Earned triumph.

cards.power: A temporary victory. You succeed today, but the future remains uncertain.
cards.lore: Equally valid as an HEA. It doesn't have to be eternal. It just has to be morally earned in this specific moment.
cards.gradeReason: Valid distinction but lore is definitional. Slightly explanatory compared to HEA's perfect mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with bittersweet watercolor. Subject: Two animals sharing a warm meal, storm clouds gathering outside. Mood: Present-tense joy.

cards.power: Destroy your public reputation to prove your private loyalty.
cards.lore: The external proof of change. The final barricade falls. Of your pride and the person. Pick one.
cards.gradeReason: 'Of your pride and the person. Pick one.' — perfect closing line. Players know the choice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Peacock stripping his feathers in a crowded plaza to defend a sparrow. Mood: Public humiliation as love declaration.

cards.power: Reveal the ultimate truth. Healing begins, but shields are gone forever.
cards.lore: The internal proof of change. The final barricade falls. The lie is dead, long live the terrifying truth.
cards.gradeReason: 'Shields are gone forever' — the cost is clear and permanent. Exactly what resolution demands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with soft watercolor. Subject: Wolf whispering into another's ear in a dark tunnel, both exhaling. Mood: Terrifying honesty.

cards.power: TRAP! If a meeting could happen to anyone, it means nothing. Discard encounter.
cards.lore: Slop symptom: The encounter is cute but arbitrary. Cure: Derive the meeting entirely from the characters' core flaws.
cards.gradeReason: 'If it could happen to anyone, it means nothing' — one sentence test for every meet-cute ever written.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with red X watercolor. Subject: Robot and person bumping into each other generically, referee throwing red flag. Mood: Generic disqualified.

cards.power: TRAP! A kiss does not fix systemic psychological damage.
cards.lore: Slop symptom: A physical act resolves a conflict that didn't earn a resolution. Cure: Every solution must cost something.
cards.gradeReason: 'A kiss does not fix systemic psychological damage' — eleven words, entire writing seminar.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Referee blowing whistle as two animals kiss, clipboard showing unresolved issues. Mood: Romantically disqualified.

cards.power: TRAP! Zero conflict means zero story. Both players fall asleep.
cards.lore: Slop symptom: Both are too competent, too kind, too agreeable. Cure: Build the Love Map and mash their trigger points!
cards.gradeReason: 'Both players fall asleep' — the joke is the rule. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Two identical sheep holding hands and snoring simultaneously. Mood: Weaponized boredom.

cards.power: TRAP! If the rival is just there to cause jealousy, the tension is fake.
cards.lore: Slop symptom: The Ex is purely a villain. Cure: The third party needs their own logic and legitimacy, or the choice has no weight.
cards.gradeReason: 'Tension is fake' — instantly diagnostic. Writers know how to fix it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: 2D cardboard cutout villain with 'RIVAL' label, protagonist sees through it. Mood: Structural embarrassment.

cards.power: TRAP! Playing the grand declaration before doing the emotional labor causes instant failure.
cards.lore: Slop symptom: The declaration is too big, too soon. Cure: Emotional escalation in microscopic steps. Save the speech for the climax.
cards.gradeReason: 'Grand declaration before emotional labor causes instant failure' — sequence is everything. Perfect gate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Bear holding roses at a first date being shown the door. Mood: Premature sincerity.

cards.power: TRAP! If the conflict can be solved with one normal sentence, it's garbage.
cards.lore: Slop symptom: Artificial silence. Cure: They cannot communicate because they don't know themselves yet, not because they dropped their phone.
cards.gradeReason: 'Not because they dropped their phone' — hilarious, specific, and exactly the rule.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Ostrich refusing to look up, holding a phone, obvious solution ignored. Mood: Manufactured silence.

cards.power: TRAP! Mentioning a dark past once and forgetting it is a storytelling felony.
cards.lore: Slop symptom: Trauma as romantic backstory jewelry. Cure: The wound MUST be actively weaponized against them at Black Moment 2.
cards.gradeReason: 'Storytelling felony' is FrizzleBob at peak. 'Must be weaponized at Black Moment 2' is exact prescription.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with handcuff watercolor. Subject: Cat wearing trauma as decorative necklace, referee writing ticket. Mood: Narrative crime scene.

cards.power: TRAP! Pretty scenery does not excuse toxic, unexamined power dynamics.
cards.lore: Stop substituting sunsets for psychological depth!! Every location must reflect the relationship dynamic, or it gets deleted.
cards.gradeReason: 'Pretty scenery does not excuse toxic power dynamics' — FrizzleBob's aesthetic manifesto in one card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Gorgeous sunset backdrop with crossed-out sign, two animals with unhealthy dynamics. Mood: Beautiful and disqualified.

cards.power: Fuel the engine with broken expectations, silence, and misread signals.
cards.lore: The pull between what they desperately want and what they are terrified to ask for.
cards.gradeReason: Definitional card — names what tension is. Lore is accurate but explanatory rather than instructional.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with stretched watercolor. Subject: Two birds pulling a rubber band between them, trembling. Mood: Taut anticipation.

cards.power: The wager is everything. Win love, or permanently lose the self.
cards.lore: If they fail, they don't just stay single. They are condemned to live forever within their own fatal flaw.
cards.gradeReason: 'Condemned to live forever within their own fatal flaw' — that is stakes. Players feel it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with void-black watercolor. Subject: Character on a scale, love on one side, the abyss on the other. Mood: Existential wager.

cards.power: Flip the paradigm. Expose that vulnerability is the ultimate armor.
cards.lore: The paradigm shift. The realization that exposing the soft underbelly is the only true show of strength.
cards.gradeReason: Correct doctrine but 'flip the paradigm' is abstract. Lore says the same thing twice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Wolf turning armor inside-out, soft lining exposed, glowing. Mood: Strength through exposure.

cards.power: Multiply attraction by the exact factor of their absolute incompatibility.
cards.lore: The cosmic joke. They are drawn to the exact person engineered to destroy their carefully curated bullshit.
cards.gradeReason: 'Engineered to destroy their carefully curated bullshit' — the entire romantic premise in one clause.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with cosmic watercolor. Subject: Cat and dog magnetically drawn together against visible warning signs. Mood: Cosmically inevitable disaster.

cards.power: Elevate the relationship from a personal crush to a universal human thesis.
cards.lore: The Love Epic. Two individuals reflecting the universal mythic hunger for connection against the void.
cards.gradeReason: 'Universal human thesis' is abstract. The aspiration is clear but hard to embody without examples.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with cosmic watercolor. Subject: Two small beetles beneath a galaxy, reaching toward each other. Mood: Cosmic intimacy.

cards.power: Combine two broken things to create an unbreakable structure.
cards.lore: Neither is whole alone. Their specific weaknesses interlock to create a structure stronger than perfection.
cards.gradeReason: 'Two broken things, unbreakable together' — the entire anti-Hallmark thesis. Instantly embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Two cracked vessels fitting together perfectly, light pouring through the joins. Mood: Kintsugi romance.

cards.power: Transformation achieved. The character can finally exist without their armor.
cards.lore: The question was never "Will they get together?" It was always "Can they mutate enough to survive the connection?"
cards.gradeReason: 'Can they mutate enough to survive the connection?' — the best definition of romance arc transformation in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with watercolor. Subject: Armored creature standing free, shed shell behind it, partner beside. Mood: Achieved transformation.

cards.power: The match ends. The Kayfabe drops. The truth emerges.
cards.lore: Truby's logic fulfilled: Moral Revelation → Moral Choice → Consequence. The Happy Ending is the ultimate moral laboratory.
cards.gradeReason: 'The Kayfabe drops. The truth emerges.' — perfect closing card. The deck eats its own framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with dawn watercolor. Subject: Two silhouettes without costumes, standing in light, revealed. Mood: Truth after performance.

verdict: This is the best pure craft deck in the corpus — a Truby-grade romance writing system disguised as a brawler. The Foul Play and Bullshit Penalties sections alone are worth the price: eight trap cards that function as a complete slop-detection workshop. Weakness: card 9 (The Contemporary Grind) has illegible power text, and the abstract 'Ghosts in the Machine' section (cards 49-52) is more definitional than performative. But the Truby Torture Rack, the intimacy trilogy, and the environmental sabotage suite are elite. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: For romance writers and story-wrestlers who want to stop explaining love and start weaponizing it. 56 cards that turn Truby's narrative theory into table moves — and call out bad craft by name.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: ROMANTIC LOVE-WRESTLING & KRASS KAYFABE-HEARTBREAKS – Romance Craft You Can Throw at a Hack (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

How many love stories have you watched stall because two grown adults refused to say one true sentence to each other?

Picture the third act you have seen a hundred times. A misheard half of a phone call. A suitcase by the door. A taxi, then a sprint through an airport that only exists because nobody finished a sentence forty minutes earlier. The genre calls this tension. It is really just two characters kept apart by bad craft, written by someone who confused withholding information with building a story. Real romance is not the absence of the fight. It is the fight that is actually worth having, run by people brave enough to stay in it.

So we pressed the whole craft of romance into fighters. Fifty-six cut-and-play cards turn Truby's narrative theory into a tag-team match: you perform the beat at the table, out loud, and the room decides whether it earns the kiss or gets booed off the mat as a cheat. This is Social Story Wrestling for everyone who has screamed "just talk to each other" at a screen and wanted the tools to write it better.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Love-Wrestling Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Comedy Shield, the joke a character hides behind so the scene never has to mean anything, Decorative Trauma, the tragic backstory bolted on for flavor that changes nothing, and The Stupid Misunderstanding, the plot that would end in one honest line and refuses to say it.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the Blödsinn! call that lets anyone at the table stop a scene the moment the romance starts lying to itself.
- The Truby Torture Engine: thirteen themed sections you run in sequence, from the Laboratory of Vulnerability and the Thunderdomes of Love through Tongue-Fu and Subtext Suplexes to the Heavyweights of Heartbreak, so a meet-cute escalates into a real reckoning instead of a montage.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
